notes: Inputs for the hay, cattle and ethanol pathway. Each names a source id, or says assumption. A late-November cow on fallout-zone pasture is the case modeled; stored hay, housed cattle and corn already in bins get far less.

interception_fraction.note: Share of falling dust caught by standing forage (EPA default for forage). Coarse explosion debris is caught less

standing_biomass_kg_m2.note: EPA default pasture yield; dormant November pasture holds less, which raises the concentration slightly

weathering_half_life_days.note: Rain and wind wash half the deposit off leaves in about two weeks (10 to 20 days in the literature)

soil_to_forage_ratio.note: Lead in plant (dry) over lead in soil (dry), forage

soil_on_hay_share.note: Soil carried on baled hay, 3.4% to 6.6% by weight depending on the rake

footprint_m2.note: Top view of a 5 by 5 foot round bale, the area dust falls on

dry_matter_kg.note: A 1,200 lb round bale at about 85% dry matter

dry_matter_intake_kg_day.note: About 2.2% of body weight for a 1,200 lb beef cow on average forage

soil_eaten_kg_day.note: EPA default for beef cattle; grazing studies find 0.1 to 1.5 kg a day

absorbed_share.note: Ruminants absorb about 4% of the lead they eat (under 2% to 15% in other sources); the rest leaves in manure

milk_transfer_d_per_l.note: Milk lead (mg/L) per mg eaten each day, at steady state

tissue_rank.note: long-term store, released slowly for months to years

cow.tissue_rank_unit: mg/kg fresh tissue per mg eaten each day, at steady state

blood_half_life_days.note: Merck gives 9 days to several months; herd studies find a median near 2 months

nrc_max_diet_mg_kg_dm.note: Maximum tolerable lead in a cattle diet, dry matter

eu_forage_mg_kg_12pct.note: EU maximum for lead in forage (hay, silage, grass) at 12% moisture

eu_feed_material_mg_kg_12pct.note: EU maximum for feed materials such as distillers grains

codex_milk_mg_kg.note: Codex maximum level for lead in milk

grain_to_soil_ratio.note: Lead in grain over lead in soil, 17 soils

foliar_to_grain_share.note: Share of lead landing on a cereal plant that moves into the grain (0.2% to 8.2%)

ddgs_concentration_factor.note: Starch becomes ethanol, so what stays in distillers grains is about 3 times as concentrated

ddgs_measured.text: 50 of 52 US corn DDGS samples had lead below 1 mg/kg; the other two had 1.0 and 1.2

per_bushel.text: A bushel makes about 2.8 gallons of ethanol and 17 lb of distillers grains

lead_boils_c.note: Ethanol boils at 78 °C, so lead does not distill over with it

iowa_harvested_pct_nov15.note: Statewide; reports say harvest near the plant was largely done

plants_nearby.text: Big River Resources, West Burlington (Des Moines County)
POET, Macon, Missouri, just south of Adair County
